candidates.title: Enhancing QUIC: Quality-of-Service LLM Serving and MASQUE Proxy Scheduling
candidates.reason: QUICのストリームスケジューリングをLLMサービングのQoSクラス別要求に合わせて設計し、深層Q学習でモデル品質を負荷に応じて切り替えるベストエフォート型サービングと組み合わせてトークンレイテンシと完了率を改善しており、サービングのスケジューリングへの直接的貢献が確認できる。

candidates.title: KV Cache Compression Based on Token-Level Redundancy Elimination and Bit-Level Encoding
candidates.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence Circuits and Systems
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) face storage and access limitations during development, requiring extensive reads of key-value (KV) cache data for each token generation. This paper designs a hardware-friendly lossless compression and decompression method for KV cache based on Token-level Redundancy Elimination and Bit-level Encoding (TREBE), reducing the amount of KV cache data that needs to be stored. In detail, token-level redundancy is first eliminated by performing subtraction between the same layers of different tokens, followed by bit-level encoding using XOR and bit-plane techniques. TREBE achieves an average compression ratio of 2.1x for the KV cache of LLaMA2-7B and OPT-6.7B models on the WikiText2 and C4 datasets, representing a 1.9x improvement over Huffman coding. With the support of TSMC 28nm process, TREBE operates at 0.9V and 0.8GHz, achieving a throughput of 6.38GB/s. Compared to Huffman coding, energy efficiency is improved by 10x, and area efficiency is enhanced by 31.2x.
candidates.reason: トークンレベルの冗長性除去とビットレベル符号化を組み合わせてLLMのKVキャッシュを圧縮する回路・システム系の手法であり、長文脈推論で支配的になるKVキャッシュ容量の削減に直結する推論向け圧縮の直接的貢献が確認できる。

candidates.title: Computationally Efficient FPGA-based Large Language Model Inference for Real-Time Decision-Making in Robotic Systems
candidates.venue: IEEE/RJS International Conference on Intelligent RObots and Systems
candidates.abstract: Integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into modern robotic systems presents significant computational and energy constraint challenges, particularly for human-centered robotic applications. This paper presents a novel hardware optimization technique for deploying LLMs on resource-constrained embedded devices, achieving an up to 77% reduction in computational latency through an FPGA implementation in comparison to other popular embedded computing devices (e.g., CPU and GPUs). Additionally, we demonstrate our methodology by deploying a LLaMA 2-7B model on a Unitree Go2 robotic dog integrated with the proposed FPGA platform. The proposed optimization framework preserves real-time interaction capabilities while significantly reducing computational and energy overhead, facilitating efficient natural language processing for human-robot interaction in safety-critical and dynamic environments. Experimental results demonstrate that the FPGA-based LLaMA 2-7B implementation achieves up to 6.06-fold and 1.95-fold higher throughput compared to baseline CPU and GPU implementations while maintaining comparable inference accuracy. Furthermore, the proposed FPGA design surpasses existing state-of-the-art FPGA implementations, delivering a 30% improvement in computational efficiency.
candidates.reason: 量子化・プルーニングとパイプライン最適化を施したLLaMA 2-7BをVersal VCK190 FPGAへ実装し、組込みCPU/GPU比で最大77％のレイテンシ削減と6.06倍のスループットを実ロボット上で示しており、オンデバイスLLM推論アクセラレーションへの直接的貢献が要旨で確認できる。
